title: Protocol to image and analyze hippocampal network dynamics in non-anesthetized mouse pups
protocol: Make a glass pipette using a 3.5″ Drummond glass pipette and a Narishgage puller (PC-100).
Cut the tip of the pipette to a diameter ranging from 25 to 40 μm.
Discard pipettes with dull openings.
Clean the injection system's pipette with alcohol.
Rinse the cleaned pipette thoroughly with sterile water or PBS.
Dry the pipette after rinsing.
Connect a silicon tube (Tygon R-3603) to the pipette.
Attach a 18G needle to the silicon tube.
Connect the 18G needle to a 10 mL syringe.
Mount the system on a stereotaxic frame (Kopf Model 940).
Dilute viral solution with 0.05% trypan blue for injection site verification.
Withdraw 2 μL of colored solution using a P20 pipette.
Place and aspirate the colored solution from parafilm.
Anesthetize newborn pups (P0.5-P1) on ice for 3-5 minutes.
Gently hold the animal's head between two fingers.
Place the pipette above the injection site.
Lower the pipette until it reaches the skin and causes a small deformation of the skull.
Zero the z-axis reference on the digital display console when piercing through the skull.
Descend to a depth of 400 μm at a speed of 150 μm/s.
Inject the viral solution at a rate of 500 nL/s, which should take approximately 10 seconds.
Check the injection position by positioning the head against a source of light and observing a "banana shape" labeling.
Warm up the pup on a heating pad set to 37°C for 2 minutes after injecting.
Rinse the pipette with sterile PBS between each injection.
Choose the more robust animal in the litter based on weight.
Wait at least 5 days between intracerebroventricular injection and surgery.
Inject subcutaneously buprenorphine at a dose of 0.05 mg/kg at the back of the neck.
Keep the pup on a heating pad for 30 minutes after analgesic injection.
Disinfect all tools with alcohol.
Cover the heating pad with a sterile diaper.
Stabilize the heat of the heating pad at 37°C.
Fix the rectal probe with tape and place it under the pup.
Place the isoflurane mask on the heating pad.
Connect a vacuum pump to a 500-mL sealed Erlenmeyer using a flexible silicon tube for aspiration.
Fix a thin pipette at the end of the tube.
Sterilize scissors in a hot bead sterilizer at 240°C for 20 seconds.
Sterilize tweezers in a hot bead sterilizer at 240°C for 20 seconds.
Rinse headplate with ethanol to remove impurities.
Rinse cannula with ethanol to remove impurities.
Set up a sterile field for cranial window surgery.
Prepare all necessary tools and materials as listed.
Apply liquid glue to the cannula previously glued with glass window.
Use a fine-tip transfer pipette for precise application of dental cement components.
Mix items for dental cement preparation according to instructions.
Keep saline solution ready on the sterile field.
Have cotton swabs available for cleaning or applying substances.
Prepare Super-Bond (Sun Medical Super-Bond C&B) for use in surgery.
Cut and lay out a piece of parafilm.
Assemble BD Microfine insulin syringe, 30 G, 0.3 mL for injections.
Set up a 26G needle with its syringe.
Place the headplate holder ready to use during surgery.
Prepare Kwik-Sil syringe for sealing purposes during cranial window creation.
Induce the pup with isoflurane at 3% in a 90% O2 / 10% air mix at a rate of 0.4 L/min for 5 min.
Transfer the pup to the heating pad set at 37°C and place its nose in the mask where the isoflurane exits.
Maintain isoflurane concentration between 0.5%‒1.5% in a 90% O2 / 10% air mix during the procedure.
Apply povidone-iodine antiseptic on the skin using a cotton swab.
Make a small midline incision between the eyes using curved scissors.
Remove the scalp above the cerebral hemispheres until lambda is reached.
Remove connective tissues with a saline-soaked cotton swab and gently push away the skin on the side.
If necessary, extend the exposed area especially on the side of the future cortectomy.
Apply a tiny amount of Super-Bond onto the skull surface and spread it out to dry for 20 s.
Wipe the surface with saline-soaked cotton swabs to remove excess liquid.
Gently scratch the skull in a grid pattern using a thin needle.
Remove impurities from the skull with a saline-soaked cotton swab and dry again.
Fix the headplate onto the skull with glue.
Apply dental cement onto the skull surface to anchor and reinforce the headplate.
Use curved scissors to cut the tip of the pipette.
Pierce the skull following the edges of the headplate using a small needle.
Lift up the skull in one piece with forceps.
Gently scratch the surface of the pia mater with a hooked needle.
Rinse and aspirate with saline.
Remove the rest of the meninges using thin forceps.
Expose the fibers from the corpus callosum.
Remove the skull over the future location of the cranial window.
Start removing the cortex from a small area.
Dig deeper until the fibers are reached on the small area.
Expand the removal area by pushing the tip forward and up.
Continue to expose the fibers by increasingly expanding the area.
Follow the direction of the fibers while removing the cortex.
Ensure that the surface is flat and there are no bleedings left before cannula implantation.
Implant the cannula and seal with dental cement if there is space between the cannula and the headplate.
Adjust focus on the aspirated area continuously.
Remove the cortex until fibers of the corpus callosum are reached.
Place aspiration tip on the lowest layer of cortex, right above the fibers.
Aspirate the cortex in the same direction as the fibers to limit damage.
Rinse until bleeding stops.
Attach forceps to the stereotaxic frame securely.
Pinch clamp ends to insert cannula.
Use pressure ends of the forceps to keep cannula in place.
Move cannula above the cortectomy.
Initiate initial descent with the cannula, stopping just after passing skull level and then returning upward.
Continuously rinse and aspirate the saline solution until bleeding stops during cannula descent.
Lay a tiny droplet of transparent silicone (Kwik-Sil WPI) onto the surface of the brain immediately after descending the cannula.
Apply slight pressure with the cannula so that the silicone droplet spreads evenly along its sides.
Ensure the thickness of the Kwik-Sil layer is minimal and does not exceed 20 seconds for descent and implantation to prevent air bubbles.
Fill any remaining space around the cannula in the craniotomy with additional Kwik-Sil if necessary.
Seal the top edge of the cannula with liquid glue attached to the headplate using a thin needle.
Pinch the end of the forceps and lift it up using the stereotaxic frame.
Stop the anesthesia and remove the animal from the isoflurane mask.
Mix saline solution or physiological serum to match the volume of buprenorphine.
Inject subcutaneously the prepared saline solution or physiological serum.
Place the pup on a heating pad at 37°C.
Allow the pup to rest on the heating pad for at least one hour.
Turn on all necessary equipment to perform imaging experiments.
Activate the laser.
Switch on the fluorescent lamp.
Start the data acquisition system.
Adjust the heating lamp to 37°C.
Initiate the xyz-stage controller.
Fix two Thorlabs optical posts onto a small aluminum Breadboard using screws.
Connect the optical posts with a third post.
Glue a small c-shaped object to one of the metallic posts.
Apply medical silicon on the entire surface of the glued object.
Place the custom saddle on the main stage underneath the objective.
Attach an infrared camera on each side directed towards the saddle.
Install the infrared light source.
Contour the outer edges of the headplate with Kwik-Sil for the pup.
Leave the Kwik-Sil to dry for 2 minutes.
Place the head-fixed mouse on the custom “saddle”.
Adjust the angles of the headpost to ensure the cannula is perfectly orthogonal to the objective.
Insert water into the cannula and verify that no air bubbles are present.
Find the surface of the hippocampus using binocular vision and a fluorescent lamp.
Start recording animal behavior.
Begin recording CA1 multi neuron dynamics.
Use a single-beam multiphoton pulsed laser scanning system coupled to a microscope (TriM Scope II, LaVision BioTec).
Set the Ti:sapphire excitation laser (Chameleon Ultra II, Coherent) at 920 nm.
Isolate GCaMP fluorescence using a bandpass filter (510/25).
Acquire images through a GaAsP PMT (H7422-40, Hamamatsu) with a 16X immersion objective (NA 0.8).
Record for a total duration of 33 minutes or 15000 frames.
Use Imspector software (LaVision BioTec) to record fluorescence activity from a 400 μm × 400 μm field of view at 9 Hz with a 1.85 μs dwell time per pixel (2 μm/pixel).
Select imaging fields of view from the dorsal CA1 area.
Maximize the number of imaged neurons in the stratum pyramidale.
Record the camera exposure time for synchronization with behavior.
Use Imspector software for data analysis.
Create a binary array with the activity of all cells as a function of time, where 1 indicates cell activity at the current frame and 0 otherwise.
Access the GPU to perform prediction of neuronal activity when using the code locally.
Follow instructions in the "inferring neuronal activity" section on the GitLab page for local usage.
Predict neuronal activity online on Google Colab if necessary.
Create a temporary Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) file at the end of this step.
Develop a graphical user interface (GUI) named CICADA for data analysis.
Accept any NWB file as input in the GUI to perform analyses.
Use BADASS analysis within the GUI to manually annotate animal behavior during imaging sessions.
Install and run the GUI following instructions provided on the GitLab repository.
Gather the segmentation and activity predictions from the temporary version.
Perform manual annotation in BADASS GUI.
Use the final NWB as input for CICADA GUI analysis.
Conduct Peri Movement Time Histogram (PMTH) analyses on the final NWB.
Display raster with behavior epochs using the final NWB data.
Generate outputs of analyses and display them.
